IDENTICAL SEQUENCE, 16-FOLD DIFFERENT LABEL. PEPlife2 assigns peptide 1 and peptide S2 the SAME sequence string, fPRPGGGGQGDFEPIPEDAYDE, yet records 13 min for one and 212.2 min for the other. The body explains the difference entirely by a modification the string does not encode: S2 'in which the second Gly residue has been replaced with a modified Lys (stearic acid)'. A sequence-to-half-life model sees two contradictory labels for one input, and the 16-fold gap is attributable to a stearoyl group that is invisible in the representation. Note also that the lowercase f in both strings marks D-Phe; the training-set sequence cleaner upper-cases it, so the D-stereochemistry is lost and the residue is read as L-Phe.

curated_notes: UNITS ERROR IN PEPlife2, now corrected. The body states the distribution half-life is 11.55 MINUTES; PEPlife2 recorded 11.55 with units 'Hours' (ID 4377), a 60-fold overstatement that also made the distribution phase eight times LONGER than the elimination phase it precedes - an impossibility the record's own numbers should have flagged. Corrected to minutes via UNITS_CORRECTIONS in subset_in_vivo_half_life.py, giving 0.1925 h. That record was in any case already excluded from the training set twice over: PEPlife2 leaves its Sequence field empty, and its phase is distribution rather than a concentration-decay terminal value. The two elimination values are NOT independent measurements: 1.45 h is the beta phase fitted over the 2-6 h window and 2.33 h is the SAME data refitted out to 12 h. The paper's own conclusion is hedged accordingly - 'the beta phase t1/2 of the tag-free rhMFG-E8 is calculated as at least 1.45 h'. Treating them as two observations double-counts one experiment and inflates the apparent spread. n is four independent experiments, not four animals.

PEPlife2 nonetheless records four half-life values against it (66.4 ± 33.0 and 40.9 ± 17.7 h, each duplicated once for the peptide-only and the peptide-plus-Fc sequence, filed as 'Rats serum'). NEITHER VALUE APPEARS IN THE BODY. The only half-life this review states for HM15136 is 'an enhanced 36 hr half-life', given without species, dose, route or citationable detail in the body text; 66.4 and 40.9 h are presumably from the primary HM15136 publication, which this review cites. Per the body-only rule these are recorded as 'not reported in body'. The values have NOT been excluded from the dataset, because they are plausibly real primary measurements; instead a source_is_review flag has been added to build_study_dossier.py and now propagates to in_vivo_half_life.csv, marking these and the 40 other records that come from the cohort's four review articles so they can be weighted or removed deliberately. Note the two PEPlife2 sequences differ (peptide alone vs peptide + IgG4 Fc) while carrying the SAME two half-lives, so this one study contributes two contradictory sequence-to-label mappings.

curated_notes: Two of three PEPlife2 values verified directly in the body: leuprolide 38.2 ± 4.3 min and LOC 172 ± 66 min. The third, 166 ± 38 min, is Table 3's value for LEUPROLIDE MEASURED AS A METABOLITE after LOC dosing (Figure 4), and PEPlife2 labels its Test Sample accordingly. That third record needs care: it is not leuprolide's own half-life - the body measures that as 38.2 min - but the apparent half-life of leuprolide released from the conjugate, which is formation-rate-limited by LOC hydrolysis and therefore tracks LOC's 172 min. Filed against the leuprolide sequence it asserts a 4.3-fold longer half-life for the same molecule. SEQUENCE DEFECT: PEPlife2 gives LOC the string HWSYlLRP while giving leuprolide pGlu-HWSYlLRP. The conjugate is leuprolide PLUS oleic acid, so its string should extend the parent's, not drop the N-terminal pyroglutamate; the oleic acid is not encoded at all. As written the conjugate looks like a truncation of the parent while carrying a 4.5-fold longer half-life. The lowercase l marks D-Leu, which the training-set cleaner upper-cases, losing the stereochemistry.

curated_notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 2.3 h is verified exactly against the Results text, for subcutaneous dosing. Note tmax is 4 h against a 2.3 h half-life, so this profile is absorption-rate-limited (flip-flop) and the value reflects depot release rather than clearance. The measurement is also strongly affected by plasma binding: total Cmax is 276 nM while FREE Cmax is 0.6 nM, a 460-fold difference, so what decays with a 2.3 h half-life is almost entirely albumin-bound material. As with PF1 in 27217590, PEPlife2 stores the sequence CYIQNCGKG - the same string it uses for PF1 - while the lipid moiety that drives the pharmacokinetics is absent; two different compounds from two different papers therefore share one representation while carrying half-lives of 2.3 h and 8.5 h. For context the paper notes native oxytocin's half-life is ~5 min and the related analogue ASK1476's is 3.2 h. No dose or group size is given in the body.

Table 3's 'Sex' column has three levels - male, female, and P - where P is the significance of the male-vs-female comparison, per the footnote 'P value: independent t test, female vs male'. Note also that the half-life here is of Gd(III), measured by ICP-MS, not of the intact peptide - the paper separately reports that the ZD2 peptide itself degrades in rat plasma with a t1/2 of 1.63 h ex vivo. THE SEQUENCE IS NOT A PEPTIDE SEQUENCE. PEPlife2 stores 'lKlW' - four characters in mixed case, marking alternating D- and L-residues - which is a monomer or repeat unit of a polymer architecture, not a molecule. The label is set by that architecture (linear vs comb vs bottlebrush spans 2.7 to >35 h for related materials), none of which the string encodes; after one-letter cleaning it becomes the four residues LKLW and the D-configuration is lost as well. The readout is also total radioactivity by scintillation counting rather than intact-species concentration, and the body gives no strain, sex, group size, dose or route.

It contributes 32 records to the cohort (30 mouse, 2 rat), the largest single review contribution, and every one of them is a value extracted from some other paper. The two rat records here, TP5-MA at 1.75 ± 0.72 h and TP5 at 0.022 ± 0.004 h, do not appear in the body text; the review's own narrative says only that unmodified peptides 'last minutes to a couple of hours'. Per the body-only rule both are recorded as not reported in body. They are NOT excluded from the dataset - they are plausibly accurate transcriptions of primary results - but they now carry the source_is_review flag added to build_study_dossier.py. Two further cautions: both records share the sequence RKDVY (thymopentin), so the 80-fold difference between them rests entirely on a modification the representation does not encode; and because a meta-analysis aggregates primary papers, these values may duplicate records the cohort already holds under their original PMIDs.

curated_notes: PEPlife2's value of 8.7 ± 2.4 h could NOT be verified numerically: the derived parameters are in a table INSET INTO FIGURE 5, which the PMC BioC deposit does not carry as text. The body confirms the qualitative claim - 'The long half time (t1/2) and the slow reduction after 12 h were observed' - and independently gives Tmax 0.83 ± 0.29 h and Cmax 8592 ± 1056 ng/mL after 10 mg/kg subcutaneous, which PEPlife2 does not record. The value is left uncorrected. STEREOCHEMISTRY LOST: PEPlife2's sequence is written entirely in lowercase, the convention marking an all-D peptide, and the body confirms DV1 is 'a novel D-peptide antagonist of CXCR4'. The training-set sequence cleaner upper-cases it, so an all-D peptide and its all-L enantiomer become the same input - while protease resistance, and therefore much of the half-life, is exactly what the D-configuration buys. The body also attributes the slow terminal phase to tissue redistribution rather than to slow clearance.

curated_notes: The single PEPlife2 value of 6.967 h is consistent with the described two-compartment analysis of gamma-counted blood radioactivity; the figure itself is not restated in the body text so it could not be checked digit for digit. Caveats. (1) n = 2 RATS per group, so no meaningful precision, and no dispersion is reported. (2) The readout is TOTAL 64Cu RADIOACTIVITY, not intact conjugate - if 64Cu dissociates from the DOTA chelator the label keeps being counted, which for copper-DOTA over a 96 h window is a real possibility. Unlike the total-radioactivity case in 36588717 the paper does not report a parent-drug comparator, so the extent of the discrepancy is unknown. (3) The stored sequence is the bare F56 peptide; the DOTA chelator, the copper and the albumin-binding CM moiety - which the introduction identifies as the half-life-extension mechanism - are all absent from it. The paper notes rat albumin's own half-life is 1.9 days.

curated_notes: All four PEPlife2 values verified exactly against the T1/2 row of Table 2 (the PEPTIDE table): 4.588, 4.25, 7.14 and 5.05 h. Two cautions. (1) PEPlife2's Test Sample strings misstate the doses - it records 'after 2.5 mg/kg sHDL-PEG2k', 'after 5 mg/kg sHDL-PEG2k' and 'after 2.5 mg/kg sHDL-PEG5k', but the body states every group received 50 mg/kg and the 5/10 figures are PEG MOL PERCENT, not doses (sHDL-PEG2k 5%, sHDL-PEG2k 10%, sHDL-PEG5k 5%); PEPlife2 appears to have halved the percentages and relabelled them mg/kg. The half-life values themselves are correct. (2) Do not confuse these with Table 3, which gives the PHOSPHOLIPID half-lives (4.59, 8.62, 9.96, 12.5 h) for the same animals - the body's headline numbers '8.6 h for sHDL-PEG2k (5%) and 12.5 h for sHDL-PEG5k (5%)' are lipid, not peptide. The paper's own conclusion is that PEGylation did NOT change peptide elimination, so the apparent 4.25-to-7.14 h spread across these four rows is within-group variability (CV up to 28.8%, n = 4), not a PEG effect. The quantified analyte deliberately includes the 22A(-)Lys metabolite.
